lines: Straight out, straight back. A good route flies true.
We made it home with everyone we left with.
The road was kinder than I expected.
I never had to reach for the bow, which suits me fine.
You kept a sensible pace the whole way.
We found shelter before the weather turned.
The path stayed clear and the string stayed dry.
I packed too many arrows and exactly enough food.
Nothing followed us past the last hill.
You listened when I asked to stop.
The village gate looked good in the evening light.
I learned the route without learning to fear it.
A quiet journey still teaches distance.
We left no gear and no one behind.
The wind was with us on the open ground.
I would take that road with you again.
Our plan held from the first step to the last.
I expected trouble and found decent weather instead.
The full quiver came home untouched.
Safe work is still good work.
That trip feathered wrong. I came home, but not without a bend in the shaft.
The wound is closed. The lesson is not.
I should have turned back when the footing changed.
You got me home after I could not keep pace.
Next time I want more bandages and fewer brave guesses.
The bow felt very heavy on the walk back.
I remember the hit more clearly than the fight.
We found cover too late to avoid trouble.
I can work again, though drawing a bow still hurts.
The healer says the scar will settle before my temper does.
I dropped half my arrows when I fell.
You carried my pack across the last field.
That road cost more than either of us planned.
I am grateful to be sore inside the village.
We need shorter watches after a fight like that.
My hands stayed steady until the danger passed.
The route home had never looked so long.
I will not ignore pain just to keep moving again.
A straight shaft can be replaced. This body gets one repair at a time.
I survived. Let us plan so survival is less difficult next time.
You loosed that hurt at close range. I will remember the aim.
I trusted you to watch my back.
Do not call it a mistake when you chose it.
The road was dangerous enough before you turned on me.
I came home without your help.
My bow was lowered because I thought you were an ally.
You knew where I was weakest and used it.
I will not travel alone with you again.
Every mile back gave me time to understand what happened.
An enemy in front of me would have been easier.
You can return the gear. You cannot return the trust.
I keep replaying the moment I stopped watching you.
The village gate felt safe because you were outside it.
I survived your choice, not your protection.
Do not ask me to forget before you have even admitted it.
I know better now than to mistake company for loyalty.
My spare string was more reliable than you.
If we speak again, keep your hands where I can see them.
The wound healed straighter than this friendship will.
You made an ally into someone who watches the door.
The boat drifted, but it did not miss the mark entirely.
Water carried us home when our legs had nothing left.
I spent the crossing keeping spray off the arrows.
The current fought every turn you made.
We should have packed a second oar.
The bow stayed wrapped until we reached shore.
I could hear trouble on the bank before I could see it.
You held the course through worse weather than I expected.
One wave nearly took the quiver.
I have never valued dry land so highly.
The river hid our tracks and carried our noise.
We waited under the bank until the wind eased.
A boat makes distance look smaller than it feels.
I trusted you with the oars while I watched the shore.
The feathers survived because we wrapped them twice.
Nothing in my pack stayed where I put it.
We reached the village wet, cold, and together.
Next trip, I choose the seat farthest from the leak.
The crossing saved time and cost me every dry sock.
I would take the boat again after we repair it.
